original_test_intent: Upgrade the NVIDIA OS driver from the recorded current version to an engineer-approved newer target, reboot as required and prove the expected module/version and every GPU/service recover without new errors.
original_method: Resolve target version/source conflict, pin signed package and compatibility matrix to exact OS/kernel/GPU, capture current version/module/DKMS/jobs/log state and known-good rollback, drain workloads, perform vendor-approved package transaction, reboot only with explicit OOB-supported approval, verify loaded module and user-space stack agree on target version, enumerate/test all GPUs and compare health/log deltas.
manual_activity: OS/GPU owner selects exact newer target/package/channel, approves outage/reboot and rollback and owns any install/boot/GPU anomaly and verdict.
required_inputs: Decision on exact target version and package/channel
Signed package/hash/signature and vendor installer option guide
Exact OS/kernel/GPU support matrix, headers/compiler/DKMS prerequisites
Current known-good driver/package/kernel and tested rollback path
Workload drain, maintenance/reboot approval and console/OOB recovery
safety_requirements: Do not download or install floating latest
Prove target is newer and compatible before mutation
Drain jobs and preserve console/OOB plus rollback
Stop on package/DKMS/module/signature/config error and do not reboot blindly
After approved reboot verify all GPUs/services/logs; no automatic reinstall or rollback
agent_execution_scope: Await target decision and validate package/system/rollback gates
Capture baseline and coordinate approved install/reboot
Verify version/module/DKMS/all-GPU health and smoke evidence
Report without deciding rollback or DUT verdict
engineer_actions: Approve drain, reboot and rollback policy

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: A post-install query does not perform or validate the source upgrade, and unsafe remote access cannot substitute for the package transaction.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: After target decision, use only the signed vendor-approved installer/package-manager flow for the exact OS/kernel; validate whether `-sb` is applicable, reboot explicitly, then verify proc/module/nvidia-smi and all GPUs.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Literal 470.57.02 filename and floating latest wording remain conflict evidence; ten-minute timings remain estimates, not target authority.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Treat the upgrade as a journaled transaction from known current to explicit target with compatibility gate, immutable package manifest, drain/install/reboot/reconnect/health checkpoints and reserved rollback.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Eliminates floating acquisition and proves the active kernel module/user-space version rather than only installer success.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A version query alone or installing the same/older version cannot satisfy upgrade coverage.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Runfile and distribution package-manager ownership may conflict; the approved channel must match existing installation provenance.

project_override_considerations: OS owner selects runfile versus distro package/DKMS policy and exact upgrade target; the review does not authorize `apt-get update` or channel mixing.
expected_evidence: Approved current-to-target decision, package signature/hash and compatibility matrix
Exact approved install argv/transaction logs and configuration-file dispositions
Reboot/OOB/reconnect timestamps and loaded kernel-module plus user-space target version
Per-GPU enumeration/smoke, services and dmesg/XID/AER/BMC/SEL deltas
Rollback readiness/use record, anomaly disposition and engineer verdict

engineering_decision_pending.question: Resolve Compatibility row247 Wistron-NV GPU-00240-V003: select the exact approved upgrade target and package channel instead of source 'latest' versus literal `NVIDIA-Linux-x86_64-470.57.02.run`; approve installer option semantics, OS/kernel/GPU compatibility, existing package ownership, DKMS/module policy, reboot and known-good rollback contract.

review_improvement: Turns a floating, potentially channel-mixing upgrade into an explicit current-to-target transaction with reboot and rollback evidence.
independent_technical_reasoning: An upgrade is relational: the target must be known and newer than the captured current version. 'Latest' changes over time, while a fixed filename can be obsolete or even a downgrade. Runfile and distro-owned drivers may conflict, and installer exit does not prove the new kernel module loaded after reboot. Therefore package provenance, module/user-space agreement and all-GPU recovery are required before an engineer can judge the result.
